name: Erumely Sree Dharmasastha Temple
significance: A Travancore Devaswom Board shrine that serves as the main gathering point for Sabarimala pilgrims on the forest route, where the Erumely Pettathullal procession is performed each pilgrimage season.

name: Agnipureeswarar Temple, Thirupugalur
deity: Shiva as Agnipureeswarar, consort Karundar Kuzhali
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam sung in the Tevaram, its masonry attributed to the 10th-century Cholas and carrying inscriptions from the reign of Uttama Chola recording tax-free grants for festivals and upkeep.
story: Agni, the fire god, is said to have worshipped Shiva at this spot, which is why the presiding deity is called Agnipureeswarar.

name: Patalesvara Siva Temple – III
deity: Shiva (lingam set in a circular yonipitha)
significance: A small sandstone pidha deul on Mandir Chowk in Old Town Bhubaneswar, near the eastern gateway of the Lingaraja temple, whose sanctum now lies about 2.6 m below the modern road and is reached by seventeen steps.

name: Nepali Mandir
significance: A carved wooden pagoda temple at Lalita Ghat begun by the exiled Nepali king Rana Bahadur Shah and completed by his son Girvan Yuddha Bikram Shah around 1843; modelled on Kathmandu's Pashupatinath and still owned by the Government of Nepal.

name: Shanmughanathar Temple, Kunnakudi
significance: A hill temple to Murugan whose 8th-century Pandya rock-cut caves preserve what are held to be the earliest sculpted dvarapalas in South Indian temple art; it is administered by the Kunnakudi Thiruvannamalai Mutt founded in the 16th century.
story: The sage Agastya is believed to have worshipped Murugan at this hill.

name: Sreevaraham Lakshmi Varaha Temple
deity: Lakshmi Varaha (Varaha with Lakshmi seated on his lap)
significance: One of only three Varaha temples in Kerala and a rare shrine showing Varaha together with Lakshmi; run by the Travancore Devaswom Board, it has a round copper-roofed sanctum and a 2.5-acre tank described as the largest temple pond in the state.

name: Vettuvan Koil
significance: An unfinished monolithic shrine cut downward into the top of a hillock under the early Pandya ruler Netunjadaiyan, the only known Pandya-era temple carved in three dimensions in situ; it is a protected monument of the Tamil Nadu archaeology department.

name: Khudneshwar Asthan Morwa
significance: A Shiva shrine in Morwa built in 1858 by the Narhan Estate; it draws crowds through the year and especially at Mahashivratri and in the month of Shravan.
story: A Muslim woman named Khudni is said to have found the lingam at the spot where her cow began yielding milk of its own accord, and the shrine carries her name.

name: Mahishasuramardini Mandapa
significance: A Pallava rock-cut cave shrine of Narasimhavarman Mahamalla's reign at Mamallapuram, part of the UNESCO-listed Group of Monuments; its three relief panels show Durga defeating the buffalo demon, the reclining Vishnu, and Somaskanda.

name: Sri Sunama Jakini Matha
deity: Sunama Jakini Mata and Malkuma Jakini Mata
significance: A modern shrine of the Suryavamshi Kshatriya Are-Katika community whose foundation was laid in February 2002 and whose consecration followed in February 2003; its annual celebrations draw an estimated 15,000-20,000 pilgrims.
story: Sunama Jakini is remembered as a devout woman buried alive on the order of her intoxicated husband around 1803 and venerated as a goddess thereafter.

name: Subarnesvara Siva Temple
significance: A 10th-century rekha deul in Bhubaneswar named for the goldsmith settlements that historically surrounded it, its decoration matching other temples of the period; seepage from the adjacent canal is now weakening its foundation.

name: Sundaresvara Siva Temple
significance: A rekha deul in Old Town Bhubaneswar dated on architectural grounds to about the 13th century, its floor set roughly a metre below the present road and reached by two flights of seven steps; it is run by a trust board under the state Endowment Department.
